summary: Round 2 re-review of all 16 units. Every round-1 fix was verified: the turning trade-off paragraph now ranks cutting speed, feed, depth for tool life and gives feed the dominant effect on Ra; the MRR example is consistent (90 m/min, 477.5 rev/min, 56.25 cm^3/min, 1.26 min); the guard-distance example gives 0.92 m and q007 gives 1.6 x 0.60 + 0.12 = 1.08 m with matching stem inputs; the tool rest, light curtain, hot-working, solid-state welding, adhesive overlap, morphological-chart, design-for-am q002 and requirements q010 edits are all accurate. Every numeric key, worked example and tolerance was recomputed in Python (spindle speed, MRR, time, Ra, heat input, weld volume and mass, bend allowance, pattern size, Chvorinov, upsetting force, FDM and build times, break-even, decision-matrix totals and sensitivity points 0.14 and 0.36, critical path and float, risk scores, grinding speed, dB sums, rivet and adhesive capacities, stock planning) and all agree with the keys. Every MCQ has exactly one defensible key. A scan of the parsed text found no tab or control characters, python format placeholders, e+06-style numbers, plain-x multiplication in LaTeX, unbraced multi-digit exponents, placeholder steps, stale option-letter references or non-ASCII garbling. Only two minor wording points remain. This is an AI review only; the course still needs a subject-matter expert (mechanical engineering and workshop safety) before engineering or safety reliance.

issues.problem: The worked example is still titled 'Guard distance and e-stop stopping time' and the S = K(t_resp + t_stop) + C model sits in the e-stop paragraph, while q007 applies it to 'the guard opening'. This formula is the presence-sensing-device (light curtain, interlock) distance model of ISO 13855; openings in fixed guards are governed by the opening-size tables of ISO 13857. The text is hedged to both standards, but the e-stop label still blurs the two. Unverified against the current standards; recommend a source check.
issues.suggestedFix: Retitle to 'Safety distance from a protective device' and state that the model applies to interlocks and presence-sensing devices; in q007 say 'protective device' rather than 'guard opening'.

issues.problem: The marking guide accepts 'increase overlap' as a measure that avoids peel. Longer overlap raises shear capacity (with diminishing returns, as the lesson now says) but does not remove peel at the overlap ends; the key-point callout also still says 'add overlap for strength' under the heading about avoiding peel.
issues.suggestedFix: Remove 'increase overlap' from the peel-avoidance measures (keep double-lap, strap, scarf, end rivet or screw, redesign so loads act in shear), and in the callout say overlap adds shear capacity only up to a point.
